title: Define multi-signal Bayesian canary + staged rollback contracts for Optimize evals
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Purpose: Produce a compact PRD that codifies acceptance contracts for Optimize eval-driven deploys. We need a deterministic, reproducible canary + staged rollback policy that uses multiple signals (automated quality metrics + safety heuristics + synthetic adversarial probes + customer telemetry) and a Bayesian stopping rule to reduce false positives while guaranteeing quick mitigation for high-impact regressions.

Scope:
- Define signal taxonomy and per-signal thresholds and weights.
- Specify stratified promptset cohorts and minimum sample sizes per cohort for statistical validity.
- Define a three-stage rollout schedule (canary -> ramp -> full) with traffic allocations and monitoring windows.
- Specify Bayesian stopping rules and decision boundaries for alarm, pause, and full rollback actions.
- Provide deterministic acceptance criteria and escalation matrix for PM/Eng/Ops.
- Backfill and retrospective requirements for post-deploy analysis.

Out of scope: detailed implementation of dashboard UI (handled by Console team) and low-level instrumentation changes (handled by runtime infra), though both are dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: All signals are enumerated with explicit success/failure directions and numeric thresholds (see signal matrix).
For each cohort, minimum sample size is defined: at least 1,000 queries or 24 hours of traffic, whichever comes first, unless customer cohort has explicit SLA requiring earlier action.

Bayesian canary actor returns posterior probability of degradation > baseline for each composite metric; action thresholds: alarm if P(degradation) >= 0.75, pause if P >= 0.9, immediate rollback if P >= 0.99 for high-impact signals.
Multi-metric decision uses weighted-sum of normalized deltas with per-metric weights configurable by project; default weight vector provided for Optimize core metrics.
A staged rollout schedule is defined: Canary 1% (4h), Canary 5% (12h), Ramp 25% (24h), Full 100% (rolling). Each stage requires no pause/rollback trigger in prior window before advancing.

Rollback triggers must include: safety fail (toxicity / PII exfiltration edge), latency SLO breach (>2x expected p50 for 95th percentile), and composite quality regression beyond Bayesian thresholds. Each trigger maps to automated actions and human-in-the-loop review items.
Runbook entries created for each action: alarm, pause, rollback, and emergency rollback. Runbooks linked in links array and validated by SRE and PM leads.
Backfill evaluation runs on a consistent promptset within 48 hours post-deploy and results posted to central dashboard with diff visualization and sample fail cases.
All above documented in a single-page PRD and reviewed/approved by Product Lead (Aisha), Runtime Lead, and SRE within two cycles.
success_metrics: False-positive automated rollback rate <= 2% across 90-day window
Mean time to detect regression (automated alarm) < 15 minutes for high-impact signals
Mean time to mitigate (automated rollback or human-confirmed rollback) < 45 minutes for high-impact incidents
No customer-seeded safety incidents post-deploy attributable to missed canary > 30 days
Canary-to-production promotion failure rate < 1% after policy adoption
signal_matrix_summary: Primary signals: 1) Quality delta (cohort A/B accuracy/utility metrics), 2) Promptset sentinel failure rate, 3) Safety classifiers (toxicity/PII), 4) Latency and error-rate SLOs, 5) Customer-side negative feedback/CS ops tickets. Each has a normalized baseline and a preferred weight; default weights: quality 0.45, safety 0.30, latency 0.15, customer_telemetry 0.10. Secondary signals include adversarial probe failures and retraining drift detectors.
cohort_specification: At minimum we require stratification by product usage pattern and prompt length: short (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), long (>512). Additional cohorts for domain-specific prompts (legal/medical/finance) must be isolated and treated with higher safety weight. Cohort-level thresholds can be stricter than global thresholds. Cohort identifiers must be embedded in eval harness metadata.
bayesian_decision_model: Use a conjugate-Beta/Gaussian posterior model per metric depending on data type. Produce posterior P(degradation >= delta_threshold) where delta_threshold is absolute effect size defined per metric. Decision bands: advisory (0.5->0.75), alarm (0.75->0.9), pause (0.9->0.99), rollback (>0.99). The model supports hierarchical pooling across cohorts to borrow strength for low-volume cohorts.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: 1% traffic for 4h; monitor windows with continuous posterior updates (every 1 minute). 2) Expanded canary: 5% for 12h if no pause/rollback; include targeted human review at +4h. 3) Ramp: 25% for 24h with automated gating. 4) Full: rolling to 100% after 48h of stable signals. At any stage, if pause or rollback threshold is triggered, halt promotion and follow runbook. Emergency rollback path bypasses approvals for critical safety or severe SLO breach.
runbook_summary: Runbook entries must include: exact metric queries, how to interpret posterior probabilities, play-by-play remediation steps, communication templates for status pages/customers, and PR/rollback checklist. Runbooks must be validated by SRE and included as links.
risks: Small cohorts may produce noisy posteriors leading to spurious alarms; mitigated by hierarchical pooling and minimum sample sizes.
Overweighting customer telemetry could trigger rollbacks due to early adopter bias; default lower weight and advisor step required for customer-driven signals.
Latency of eval harness (backfill) might delay backfill analyses; we require compute budget commitment and TTL for backfill jobs.
Misconfigured adversarial probes could generate targeted false negatives; we will maintain a curated adversarial library and review cadence.
dependencies: Console: dashboard widgets for posterior time series and sample-case drilldowns
Runtime infra: hooks for staged traffic routing and emergency rollback API
Eval infra: promptset cohort tagging and backfill compute slots
SRE: runbook review and on-call escalations
Legal/Privacy: review for PII detection thresholds
notes: This PRD consolidates several prior threads that proposed purely frequentist thresholds; the Bayesian approach is chosen to give calibrated uncertainty and lower false-positive rollbacks.
We default to conservative action thresholds; projects with high tolerance for quality regression may opt to relax alarms with cross-functional approval.
Plan includes a two-week pilot using internal traffic and synthetic adversarial probes before customer-facing canaries.
